blocks.text: You can search logs ingested from sources connected to the Agentic Security Operations Platform (Agentic SecOps Platform) on the Logs page. You can use the basic query builder or write more complex analytical queries using an advanced query builder to search for specific log records and investigate critical information quickly.

blocks.item: Build a Basic Query

The basic query builder is a visual tool that makes it easy to explore logs and add filter conditions. Security analysts can use this tool to review logs for specific events, gather evidence for auditors, or troubleshoot configuration or mapping issues.
To build a basic query:
In the Agentic SecOps Platform Admin Portal, click Explore.
In the left-side navigation, click Logs.
See image.
Click the + icon to add a new query tab.
If you have not previously created a query, you can select a prebuilt query from the list to get started or click Library and select a saved query.
See image.
To filter results to a specific time frame, use the time filter. To learn more, see Using Filters.
The selected time frame is not saved as part of the query, and must be configured for every result.
To filter results by source, select one or more from the Sources list.
To add other filter conditions, click the Search Logs field to open the query builder.
See image.
Select a field or enter a field name manually.
Select an operator (e.g., Equals, Contains, Starts With, etc.).
Enter or select the value you want to filter by.
(Optional) Use AND or OR operators to add conditions to the query.
(Optional) Click Save to save your query to the Queries Library.
Click Search.
The query results appear.
(Optional) Click Export as CSV to export the data as a CSV file.
See image.
Build an Advanced Query

You can use the advanced query builder to write queries using PostgreSQL syntax. This allows you to have control over search logic to perform complex analysis, such as joins, nested queries, and aggregations, or who need access to a function library for dynamic data processing (e.g., string and date manipulation, aggregate or window functions).
To create an advanced query:
In the Agentic SecOps Platform Admin Portal, click Explore.
In the left-side navigation, click Logs.
See image.
Click the + icon to add a new query tab.
In the query builder, click Basic to switch from basic to advanced mode.
To filter results to a specific time frame, use the time filter. To learn more, see Using Filters.
The selected time frame is not saved as part of the query, and must be configured for every result.
To view the available tables and columns you can reference in your query, search for or click a source in the Tables section.
A drawer opens with details about the source.
Click Query this table to generate a sample SQL query.
The sample query replaces the current query on the Query tab.
See image.
In the query field, modify the sample query as necessary.
Click Search.
The query results appear.
(Optional) Click Export as CSV to export the data as a CSV file.
See image.
Add a Query to the Queries Library
The Queries Library includes all saved queries. You can save queries and add them to the library for quick access.
To add a query to the Queries Library:
After creating a query, click Save at the top right of the page.
See image.
The Edit Details window appears.
In the Edit Details window, enter a name for the query and add a description.
Click Save.
The query is saved to the library.
See image.
(Optional) Click Save as New to update the existing query and save it as a new query.
See image.
To run a saved search:
On the Logs page, click Library.
The Queries Library window appears.
In the Queries Library window, click the query you want to search for.
Click Search.
The query results appear.
Filter Search Results

After you run a search for a query, results appear under the query field. Click a record to review the fields in a drawer. You can search for a specific field, or copy all the fields using the Copy Log icon in the top-right corner.
See image.
Hover over a field in the drawer to display the following icons:
Remove Column: Hide a column in the log table.
Copy Value: Copy the value of the field.
Analyze Data
You can filter and analyze the query results using the Time Series chart or Pie Chart.
The Time Series chart shows the number of logs (on the y-axis) that match the query conditions, retrieved from your sources within the time frame selected in the time filter.
See image.
You can click and drag the time filter to select a portion of the chart to define your desired time frame. This updates the table view as shown in the following image.
See image.
The selected time filter is not saved as part of the query, and must be configured each time.

The Pie Chart displays all logs filtered by your query. Use the Breakdown by drop-down menu to select the field you want the logs to be grouped in, and the number of top values you want to be presented in the legend.
See image.
Select any number of slices to filter by their value. This also adds your selection as a filter in the table of logs.
See image.
To remove a value from the filter created by the pie chart, deselect the slice on the chart itself or click the Remove slicer icon under the chart.
See image.
